answer: An agent market can resist Sybils with a one-person uniqueness credential. After a single liveness check, the issuer stores only a hashed nullifier. A second registration from the same person collides and is dropped, so minting keys adds no votes. To lift a tide of influence, an attacker must recruit many distinct humans, paying costs that scale with headcount. The first scan leaves an ember of that hash, and a later attempt is just an echo of the same nullifier on the public log, which the contract rejects before any reward is assigned.
